nodes.summary: A codon: three nucleotides, each in `Fin 4` (order `A, C, G, T`).
nodes.title: Codon as a triple of nucleotides

nodes.summary: `dN / dS = ω` in the Goldman–Yang model with sites counted under `ω = 1` (derived; see the module docstring for the site definition), provided `ρ_S(1) > 0` and `ρ_N(1) > 0`.
nodes.title: `dN / dS = ω`

nodes.summary: The nonsynonymous rate per nonsynonymous site, `dN = ρ_N(ω) / N`.
nodes.title: Nonsynonymous substitution rate per nonsynonymous site (dN)

nodes.summary: The synonymous rate per synonymous site, `dS = ρ_S(ω) / S`.
nodes.title: Synonymous substitution rate per synonymous site (dS)

nodes.summary: The positions at which two codons differ.
nodes.title: Positions at which two codons differ

nodes.summary: The nonsynonymous exchangeabilities are linear in `ω`, the synonymous ones do not involve it.
nodes.title: Dependence of Goldman–Yang exchangeabilities on ω

nodes.summary: The Goldman–Yang exchangeabilities are symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of Goldman–Yang exchangeabilities

nodes.summary: The Goldman–Yang exchangeability between codons `i` and `j`: `0` unless they differ at one position; otherwise `κ` for a transition (`1` for a transversion), times `ω` if the amino acid changes.
nodes.title: Goldman–Yang codon exchangeability

nodes.summary: Off the diagonal the Goldman–Yang rate is `gyExchange i j * π j`.
nodes.title: Off-diagonal entries of the Goldman–Yang rate matrix

nodes.summary: The Goldman–Yang rate matrix (Goldman & Yang 1994): the GTR matrix with codon frequencies `π` and exchangeabilities `gyExchange`.
nodes.title: Goldman–Yang codon rate matrix

nodes.summary: It is in detailed balance with its codon frequencies.
nodes.title: The Goldman–Yang chain is reversible

nodes.summary: With nonnegative frequencies, `κ ≥ 0` and `ω ≥ 0`, the Goldman–Yang matrix is a rate matrix.
nodes.title: Goldman–Yang matrix is a rate matrix

nodes.summary: Differing at exactly one position is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of single-position codon changes

nodes.summary: Two codons differ at exactly one position.
nodes.title: Codons differing at exactly one position

nodes.summary: Being a transition change is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of transition codon changes

nodes.summary: Every differing position is a transition (same parity: `A ↔ G` or `C ↔ T`).
nodes.title: Codon change consisting of transitions

nodes.summary: The nonsynonymous rate is linear in `ω`: `ρ_N(ω) = ω ρ_N(1)`.
nodes.title: Nonsynonymous rate is linear in ω

nodes.summary: `ρ_N(1) > 0` if the frequencies are nonnegative, `κ > 0`, and some nonsynonymous single change joins two codons of positive frequency.
nodes.title: Positivity of the nonsynonymous rate

nodes.summary: The stationary rate of nonsynonymous substitutions per codon, `ρ_N = ∑_{aa i ≠ aa j} π_i Q_ij`. This is the stationary rate when `∑ i, π i = 1`; for unnormalized weights it is scaled by `(∑ i, π i) ^ 2`.
nodes.title: Stationary rate of nonsynonymous substitutions

nodes.summary: The number of nonsynonymous sites per codon, counted under `ω = 1`: `N = 3 ρ_N(1) / (ρ_S(1) + ρ_N(1))`.
nodes.title: Number of nonsynonymous sites per codon

nodes.summary: The synonymous rate does not depend on `ω`: `ρ_S(ω) = ρ_S(1)`.
nodes.title: Synonymous rate does not depend on ω

nodes.summary: `ρ_S(1) > 0` if the frequencies are nonnegative, `κ > 0`, and some synonymous single change joins two codons of positive frequency.
nodes.title: Positivity of the synonymous rate

nodes.summary: The stationary rate of synonymous substitutions per codon, `ρ_S = ∑_{i ≠ j, aa i = aa j} π_i Q_ij`. This is the stationary rate when `∑ i, π i = 1`; for unnormalized weights it is scaled by `(∑ i, π i) ^ 2`.
nodes.title: Stationary rate of synonymous substitutions

nodes.summary: There are three sites per codon: `S + N = 3` when `ρ_S(1) + ρ_N(1) ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Synonymous and nonsynonymous sites sum to three

nodes.summary: The number of synonymous sites per codon, counted under `ω = 1`: `S = 3 ρ_S(1) / (ρ_S(1) + ρ_N(1))`.
nodes.title: Number of synonymous sites per codon

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
